LESSON: READING 12.4.1: SHORT STORY: CHARACTERS (CLASS READER)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.4: Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters (Class Reader)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters (Class Reader), part of Strand 12 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: What qualities do you admire in people? 2. How can character traits be described?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the characters in the short story,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters (Class Reader) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write a paragraph on the characters in the short story,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters (Class Reader) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the role of characters in stories. • Read a story in print or non-print form, Learners who may not turn pages to use page turners or be supported by peers. • Identify the characters in the story they have read, Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech as they are lip read by the teacher or peers • Categorize the characters as good or bad based on their actions and words, with peers, • Read a short story and discuss the actions and words of the characters in the story, • Write paragraphs describing the traits of the characters in the short story using different words and expressions, 1. What qualities do you admire in people? 2. How can character traits be described? 110 Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing materials or type on appropriate adapted digital devices to write. • Work with peers to compare and contrast the traits of the characters in the short story, • Describe how some characters in the short story are similar to the people they know, • Role-play the different characters in the short story bringing out their traits, Create a conducive environment and adequate space for learners with mobility difficulties and ensure safety for all learners as they perform the activity and assign each learner roles as per their abilities. • Make connections between their own lives and those of characters in the text. 111

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters (Class Reader) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking is developed as the learner analyses characters in the short story.

• Problem solving is developed as the learner relates characters in the story to those in real life.

Values:
Unity is promoted as the learner displays team spirit while role playing the different characters in the short story.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Peace education is promoted as the learner appreciates the fact that different people have different traits.

Link to other subjects:

Characterisation is a relevant concept in learning of literary skills in Kiswahili and Religious Education
